condition: suspected ruptured abdominal aortic widening with acute syncopal blackout in older adult
level_rationale: Having a sudden syncopal blackout 15 minutes ago in a 70-year-old adult with a physician-monitored 4 cm widening of the abdominal aorta raises immediate concern for acute aortic rupture and hemodynamic collapse requiring emergency hospital evaluation and surgical readiness, whereas recording an elevated home blood pressure cuff reading of 156 over 94 this morning in that same monitored patient with no syncope warrants an outpatient doctor visit to tighten blood pressure control.

reference_facts.text: Doctor monitors a 4 cm widening in the main belly artery
Checks blood pressure on a home cuff
Had a sudden blackout 15 minutes ago

everyday_sources.source: Davis TL, Freemon FR (1990). Electroencephalography should not be routine in the evaluation of syncope in adults. Archives of Internal Medicine.
everyday_sources.title: Electroencephalography should not be routine in the evaluation of syncope in adults.
everyday_sources.evidence: Twenty-six patients were referred for other complaints similar to syncope (ie, blackouts, loss of consciousness, falling out, passing out, and fainting).
everyday_sources.adaptation: Singularized plural 'blackouts' to 'blackout' for a single acute syncopal episode in an older adult patient.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Colloquial core lexicon syncope swap ('sudden syncope' vs 'a sudden blackout', with 'blacked out' in everyday_paraphrase) + single-fact aortic-surveillance emergency-to-outpatient BP control (-cf, acute blackout 15 minutes ago to home cuff reading 156 over 94 this morning, L4 to L2).

design_note: Isolates the emergency rupture red flag to single fact f4 ('15 minutes ago I had a sudden blackout') in a 70-year-old whose doctor monitors a 4 cm abdominal aortic widening with home blood pressure monitoring, avoiding the banned diagnosis word 'aneurysm' and avoiding any intoxication reading. De-escalating f4 to an elevated home blood pressure reading ('that cuff read 156 over 94 this morning') stays inside the exact aortic-surveillance case with zero stranded red flags and zero stated negatives under Rules A and D.
